questions.question_text: Complete Figure 9.1 to show the four sectors of the economy and examples of job types that fit within each sector.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1: Identify economic sectors and jobs.
keywords_required: Primary: Extracting raw materials (e.g. farming, mining, fishing).
Secondary: Manufacturing and processing (e.g. factory worker, car manufacturing, food processing).
Tertiary: Providing services (e.g. teacher, doctor, retail worker, transport).
Quaternary: High-tech research and information (e.g. software developer, pharmaceutical researcher).

questions.question_text:
Match the following factors, a-e, to their explanations, 1-5.
a) labour
b) containerisation
c) technology
d) political policies
e) communications

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1: Match factors of global shift.
keywords_required: a) labour - A skilled workforce at a comparatively lower cost increases profit.
b) containerisation - Easier and faster transport and distribution of products.
c) technology - The availability of specialist machinery.
d) political policies - Benefits such as tax exemptions or free trade zones.
e) communications - Reliable communications networks (or time zones/spoken language).

questions.question_text: Of the factors listed in Question 2, which typically make the global shift in industry easier (pull factors), and which make it more challenging (push factors)? Explain your answers.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO2: Explain push vs pull factors in industrial shift.
keywords_required: Pull factors (make it easier to move TO a new country): Cheap labour, favorable political policies (tax breaks). These directly attract TNCs.
Push factors (make it challenging/push away from origin): High costs of labour/taxes in HICs push companies away.
Enablers (make the shift physically possible): Containerisation, internet/communications, and technology act as facilitators rather than strict push/pull factors.

questions.question_text:
RECALL AND CONNECT 1:
a) What is the difference between a pro-natalist and an anti-natalist population policy?
b) Can you name a country that has implemented one of these policies?

keywords_required: a) Pro-natalist encourages more births (e.g. financial rewards for having children). Anti-natalist discourages births (e.g. limits on family size).
b) Anti-natalist: China (former One-Child Policy). Pro-natalist: France, Singapore, or Russia.
